archetypes.name: token-render-pipeline
archetypes.rationale: The plan introduces a substitution token READABILITY_STYLE for external-agent prompts but never identifies which script or code path expands that token at runtime; if no renderer performs the substitution, agents receive the literal token string and the feature is silently inert.
archetypes.prompt_body: Investigate whether any script in skills/design/scripts/ or the design skill's reference-rendering pipeline currently performs variable substitution when writing slot prompts such as BRAINSTORM_FRAMING_PROMPT, ARCH_PROMPT, and INNOVATION_PROMPT to disk or to agent input. Determine whether a substitution mechanism already exists, is implied by the plan but left unspecified, or is entirely absent. If no expansion step is described or present, that is a critical plan gap: every amended prompt file will contain the literal text READABILITY_STYLE rather than the preamble content. Also check whether the plan correctly distinguishes which sites need token substitution versus MANDATORY read directives, and whether any site appears to be misclassified between the two mechanisms. Cite specific file paths and line ranges for any issues found, and follow the output-format rules from your outer wrapper exactly.

archetypes.name: amendment-coverage
archetypes.rationale: The plan lists eight amendment sites but does not verify exhaustiveness against the full set of user-facing writing sites in the design skill; other SKILL.md step bodies, helper scripts, or reference files may generate operator-visible prose and would be silently exempt from the style preamble.
archetypes.prompt_body: Read skills/design/SKILL.md completely and map every step or sub-step that produces operator-visible prose against the plan's eight listed amendment sites. Identify any step bodies, reference files, or scripts under skills/design/ that generate user-facing text but are absent from both the plan's amendment list and the lint manifest. Pay particular attention to AskUserQuestion label and description text, Gate A, Gate B, and Gate C confirmation prose, Step 1b and Step 1c pre-discussion text, and any Step 5 output paths beyond composed-plan.md. Cite specific file paths and line ranges for any issues found, and follow the output-format rules from your outer wrapper exactly.

archetypes.name: lint-manifest-soundness
archetypes.rationale: The lint uses a hard-coded manifest and two distinct grep patterns; if the patterns are too loose, if newly created files are not self-referentially included or excluded correctly, or if the two-pattern assignment between orchestrator-inline and external-agent sites is wrong, the lint can pass while coverage silently erodes.
archetypes.prompt_body: Examine the plan's specification of lint-readability-preamble.sh and assess whether the hard-coded manifest should include or exclude the new files created by this change, particularly readability-style.md itself, and whether checking the preamble file for its own token would be circular. Evaluate whether the two grep patterns, one for the substitution token and one for the MANDATORY directive, are precise enough to avoid false positives from example text, comments, or documentation prose. Check that the test harness in test-lint-readability-preamble.sh exercises the non-compliant branch for each pattern variant separately, not only for one variant. Also verify the Makefile wiring adds the new targets to the correct dependency chain so the lint runs as part of the pre-commit hook suite. Cite specific file paths and line ranges for any issues found, and follow the output-format rules from your outer wrapper exactly.
